**VitaFlavor Inc. - Q3 2023 Earnings Call Transcript**

**Operator:**  
Good morning, and welcome to the VitaFlavor Inc. Q3 2023 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. The floor will open for questions at that time, and instructions will be provided then. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Emily Carter, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

**Emily Carter (Head of Investor Relations):**  
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss VitaFlavor Inc.'s Q3 2023 results. Joining me on the call are Alex Rivera, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Thompson, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Chen, Chief Growth Officer; and David Patel, Chief Supply Chain Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call may contain forward-looking statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a discussion of the factors that could cause actual results to differ materially from these statements.

With that, I'll turn the call over to Alex Rivera.

**Alex Rivera (CEO):**  
Thank you, Emily, and good morning, everyone. We are pleased to report our results for Q3 2023. We delivered strong performance despite ongoing macroeconomic headwinds and inflationary pressures.

Today, I'll be focusing on five key areas: organic revenue growth overall and by region, performance of key brands and product categories, market share trends for major brands, progress on sustainability initiatives and goals, and discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies.

First, regarding organic revenue growth overall and by region. Our organic revenue growth came in at 5.4% year-over-year on a reported basis, excluding the effects of foreign exchange, acquisitions, and divestitures. This represents our sixth straight quarter of positive organic growth, surpassing the Food & Beverage industry average of 2-3% according to NielsenIQ and IRI data. The growth stemmed from a balanced combination of 2.1% volume increases, 2.8% from pricing actions, and 0.5% from favorable product mix shifts, showcasing our disciplined approach amid input cost inflation and evolving consumer preferences.

This momentum built on our constant-currency organic growth, which sped up from 4.2% in Q2, propelled by outperformance in non-alcoholic beverages and savory snacks, where we picked up 110 basis points of global market share. Underpinning this were initiatives like our AI-driven demand forecasting platform, which boosted inventory turns by 15% and cut stockouts by 22% throughout the supply chain—essential given volatility in commodities such as cocoa, coffee, and aluminum. Our premiumization efforts, moving 12% of the portfolio to higher-margin items like plant-based protein shakes and zero-sugar functional beverages, generated 180 basis points of mix benefit, in line with trends at companies like Monster Beverage and Celsius Holdings.

By region, our growth profile stays balanced. In North America, which accounts for 45% of total revenue, we saw solid 3.2% organic growth, edging out the 2.8% category average from Circana data. Volumes were nearly flat at 0.1%, offset by 3.1% pricing to counter 8-10% COGS inflation from dairy and corn. Standouts included the HydraFuel electrolyte line, up 14% thanks to distribution into 2,500 additional Walmart and Kroger stores, riding the hydration surge post-pandemic much like Gatorade. E-commerce now makes up 18% of North America sales, up from 14% a year ago, via direct-to-consumer ties with Instacart and Amazon Fresh. We're emphasizing health-focused positioning with low-calorie, high-protein snacks to fend off private labels, maintaining 62% all-commodity volume penetration.

In EMEA, 25% of revenue, we achieved standout 6.8% organic growth, far exceeding the 1.5% regional industry mark despite sugar taxes in the UK and France. Pricing drove 4.2%, implemented proactively against regulations, with volumes up 2.1% from innovation. The GreenWave organic tea lineup jumped 22%, grabbing share in the €15 billion ready-to-drink tea space versus Unilever's Lipton, boosted by sustainable sourcing certifications that appeal to EU shoppers—80% of whom prioritize ESG factors per Kantar. Savory nut mixes expanded into 1,200 Lidl and Tesco doors, countering a 3% dip in carbonated soft drinks from health shifts. Our Amsterdam R&D hubs are speeding up better-for-you reformulations, such as stevia-sweetened colas, to meet EU 2025 front-of-pack labeling.

Asia-Pacific, 18% of revenue, powered ahead at 9.1% organic growth, fueled by urbanization and rising middle-class demand in India and Indonesia. Volumes rose 5.4%, beating the 4% category pace, with modest 3.2% pricing for affordability. ZenEnergy ready-to-drink coffees grew 28% in China through Tmall and JD.com deals, akin to Red Bull but with adaptogens for wellness. In India, sachet packs for salty snacks took 150 basis points in the ₹50,000 crore namkeen market, aided by festive demand. We're building cold-chain logistics with partners like Swiggy, lifting out-of-stock recovery to 95%, while increasing hedging coverage by 20% against rice and palm oil swings.

Latin America, 10% of revenue, posted robust 7.5% growth despite currency issues and 12% inflation in Brazil and Mexico. Aggressive 4.8% pricing paired with steady 2.4% volumes, led by treats. TropiCrunch fruit gummies expanded 19% into 3,000 Soriana and Chedraui stores in Mexico, hitting the $10 billion confections space. Low-sugar yogurts gained in Brazil amid recovery, similar to Danone. Route-to-market tweaks via micro-depots raised rural reach by 8%, vital in fragmented areas, with palm oil hedging softening 15% cost fluctuations.

Rest of World, 2% of revenue, grew 4.2%, mainly from Middle East energy drink distribution.

Moving ahead, we anticipate Q4 organic growth of 5-7%, led by APAC and EMEA as comparisons ease. Our three-pillar approach—innovation with 15% of sales from launches under three years, distribution targeting plus-1 point ACV gains, and efficiency through the BevOptix ERP upgrade—equips us against softening sentiment and recession risks. We're growing profitably, with organic gross margins up 120 basis points to 42.1%.

Second, concerning performance of key brands and product categories. Our segments showed organic net revenue growth of 7.2%, beating the industry 4.1% per IRI and Nielsen. This came from 3.8% volume and 3.4% pricing, strongest in premium health items amid premiumization.

Breaking it out: Beverages, 52% of revenue, hit 9.5% organic growth with share gains in still and sparkling. PureSip, our top non-carbonated brand including PureSip Hydrate with electrolytes and vitamins, rose 12.3% on 8.2% volume, taking 1.7 share points in North America per Nielsen. Velocity shone in convenience and e-com, with 92% ACV up from 87%. Carbonated FizzWave grew 6.8%, with 4.1% pricing against aluminum and HFCS costs, volumes flat at 0.2%, gaining 0.9 points in EMEA versus Coke and Pepsi via FizzWave Zero Sugar down 30% in sugars for EU labels. APAC led at 14.2% from iced teas in China and India, like Mondelez emerging plays. EBITDA margins up 120 bps to 28.4% from aseptic lines in Mexico cutting waste 15%.

Snacks & Confectionery, 28% of revenue, delivered 5.9% organic growth, shifting to better-for-you against salty softness. CrunchyBites savory baked chips and nut clusters grew 7.4% on 4.6% volume, up 1.2 points to 14.8% U.S. share in $32B category. CrunchyBites Protein Packs with 10g protein per serving tripled velocity in Costco and Sam's. Pricing at 2.8% handled wheat and oil inflation via algorithms. SweetBurst gummies and chocolates rose 3.2% versus 1.1% contraction, premium organic/low-glycemic. LATAM ACV to 78% with 1,200 points, like Hershey regionally. EBITDA steady at 24.7%, $15M savings from palm hedging and Brazil regen ag.

Nutritionals & Convenience Foods, 20% of revenue, accelerated to 8.7%, tapping $200B plant-based/functional per Euromonitor. DairyDelight yogurt and alt-dairy up 11.2% on 7.9% volume, plant oat yogurts taking 2.1 points from Chobani/Danone. FlexFuel RTD shakes with collagen/adaptogens grew 25% e-com on Amazon/Instacart, online F&B up 40% YoY. QuickNourish frozen meals up 6.1%, 3.5% pricing vs protein/logistics. EMEA 9.8% post-HFSS reformulations to 100-cal servings. APAC 13.4% localized ramen/meal kits like Nestle Maggi. EBITDA up 180 bps to 32.1% from precision fermentation cutting pea protein COGS 20%.

Strategically, Health Horizon commits $250M over three years for R&D/sustainability, 50 new 2024 SKUs like zero-cal sodas/upcycled snacks for 15% CAGR BFY. North America 55% sales up 6.8%, e-com 18%; EMEA 20% 8.9% vs FX; APAC 15% 12.4% urbanization; LATAM 10% 7.2%. Divested low-growth brands for $180M, into M&A like Korean kombucha stake. AI forecasting cut stockouts 22% like P&G. Q4 category 7-9%, FY organic 7.5%, EBITDA +100 bps to 26.5%.

Third, in terms of market share trends for major brands. Across major brands, this is central to growth in competitive F&B. Our Health Forward, Flavor First platform drove steady gains despite category volume softness and inflation.

Per latest Nielsen/IRI through Q3 end, total company share hit 14.2% in core F&B markets, up 110 bps YoY from 13.1%—11th straight quarter, vs category -1.8%. Gaining from private labels down 80 bps on quality issues and peers with execution slips.

Beverages, 42% revenue: AquaPure sparkling and ZestEnergy functional up 1.9 points to 16.7% NARTD. AquaPure +3.2 to 22.4% enhanced water, taking 1.5 from Pepsi Bubly via BerryCitrus Zero with 50% more electrolytes/stevia, 15% ACV in eight weeks. ZestEnergy +2.1 to 11.3% energy, closing on Monster 28% with 14% c-store velocity, IRI household +14%. ASP flat $1.85 vs 4.2% category inflation for trial.

Snacks & Confectionery 35%: NutriCrunch bars/BlissChoc +0.8 to 12.9% vs -2.1% category. NutriCrunch +1.4 to 18.2% protein snacks, beating Mars Kind with 25g plant protein 20% cheaper, ACV 62% mass. BlissChoc 9.8% premium choc, +0.6 from Hershey via Amazon +35% velocity, AR campaigns +18% conversion. Down 0.3 vs Mondelez Oreo, fixing with $50M savory-sweet Q1.

Dairy & Plant-Based 18%: VitalCream oat milk/yogurts +1.6 to 10.4%, plant dairy 14% volume per Circana. VitalCream +2.7 to 15.1% over Chobani plant, B2B foodservice +28%, regen sourcing. Europe sugar taxes -0.4, offset U.S.

Regionally: North America 65% +1.7 to 17.3%, club bundles +25% velocity vs Coke Dasani. EMEA 18% flat 11.2% vs Unilever Ben & Jerry's, 40% reformulated HFSS. APAC 12% +2.4 to 9.8%, ZestEnergy +4.1 China Tmall vs Red Bull. LATAM 5% +0.5 to 7.1%, Brazil ethanol low-cal.

Initiatives: Premiumization 65% gains $2+ ASP, health claims 2x loyalty per LoyaltyOne. Tech distribution AI routes 92% shelf, +450 bps IRI, DoorDash/Instacart 45% sales. Sustainability 70% carbon-neutral ahead Nestle, RepTrak +12.

FY share +100-150 bps if costs moderate (cocoa -8%, dairy stable). $300M pipeline GLP-1 snacks de-risks private label.

Fourth, looking at progress on sustainability initiatives and goals. Sustainability is integral to value creation, embedded in FY24 priorities across sustainable sourcing, emissions reduction, water stewardship, and circular packaging.

Sustainable sourcing: 78% key inputs (cocoa, palm, coffee, dairy) verified sustainable, up from 62%, beating 75% FY24 target ahead of Mondelez 72%. Regenerative Ag Program 450,000 hectares with Savanna Institute. North America 30% Midwest corn no-till, +1.2t soil carbon/ha via Control Union. Europe 92% palm RSPO for EU Deforestation Reg. APAC 150 smallholders blockchain-traceable tea, 100% deforestation-free like Nestle Farmer Connect.

Emissions: Scope 1/2 -22% to 1.45M tCO2e, on SBTi 45% cut by 2030 from 2019. Scope 3 -18% via suppliers, 65% renewable power, solar 40% LATAM bottling like Pepsi gigaton. Memphis plant digesters 95% methane capture, 15% energy, ROI <3 yrs.

Water: Efficiency +28% to 1.8L/L beverage, over 25% goal. India Rajasthan zero-discharge 98% recycle with IDE. 55% sites water positive, $12M California aquifers.

Circular packaging: 62% recyclable/reusable/compostable up from 48%, Ellen MacArthur aligned. 100% rPET TerraSparkle bottles Europe/NA -35k tons virgin. UK Loop reusable ready-meals -40% single-use. Landfill 4.5% from 12%, food waste 92% diversion Too Good To Go.

Europe pacesetter 95% CSRD, +8% organic premium sales. NA Green Thumb pea-protein TerraBars +5 share IRI. APAC/LATAM scaling, $50M Indonesia palm financing. Delivers $145M savings, NPS +12% Gen Z 35% volume Kantar. Buffered cocoa crisis diversified. Net-zero 2042, 100% sustainable 2030, $1B green capex hydrogen fleets. Scope 3 transport +3% freight stubborn, but CDP A-list.

Fifth, reviewing discussion of pricing actions and revenue growth management strategies. Pricing and RGM are foundational, blending elasticity, mix, promotions, volume in volatile costs/consumer shifts. Net revenue +8.2% YoY, pricing 5.5 pts, volume 1.2%, mix 1.5 pts—sixth quarter positive volume, beating Pepsi/Keurig trends.

Strategic pricing: Avg 6.1% hikes via AI engine on 15M+ loyalty/Nielsen/IRI data, SKU-store elasticity with CPI (NA 3.1%, EM 7-9%).

Beverages 55%: 5-7% on CSDs like Zesty Cola 40% share, functional waters. Elasticity -1.8, premium RTD VitaBoost +12% sales 8% price -1.2 elasticity, millennial health Ozempic trade-up.

Snacks 35%: 4-6% salty/nutrition, cocoa +45% West Africa. NutriCrunch plant protein +7% flat volume, BFY +15% dollars vs flat category. Penetration 68% top SKUs Kantar, minimal private label loss vs Coke 2-3%.

Regions: NA 65% 5.8% club/e-com EDLP trade -120 bps to 22%, convenience +2.1% vs +0.5% IRI. Europe 20% 4.2% HFSS shrinkflation biscuits/RTD teas +3% zero-sugar like Unilever. EM 15% 9.5% Brazil sachets +18% vol 11% inflation Nestle Maggi.

RGM tech: VitalRGM ML SAP/CDP +15-20% promo ROI, -25% bad coupons geo/AI, dynamic pilots 5k Walmart/Kroger +2-3% elasticity. Zero-based trade -200 bps FY24 to 20%.

Premiumization/right-sizing premium mix 28-32% +12% ARPU, offsets dairy +8%/corn +6%, ESG Rainforest 70% cocoa. H2 4-6% pricing, RGM 7-9% revenue stable FX no recession, elasticity -1.5--2.0.

Overall, we are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael Thompson to provide more detail on our financial results.

**Michael Thompson (CFO):**  
Thank you, Alex. As Alex mentioned, we achieved solid results in Q3 2023. Net sales were $2.8 billion, representing a 7.2% increase year-over-year. Gross margin was 42.1%, benefiting from pricing discipline, mix shift, and supply chain efficiencies despite commodity pressures. Operating income was $480 million, up 10% from last year, and diluted earnings per share were $1.42. We are managing our costs effectively and continue to invest in key growth initiatives.

Our balance sheet remains strong with $1.6 billion in cash and marketable securities. We are committed to returning value to shareholders through dividends and share repurchases, having executed $100 million in dividends and $200 million in buybacks this quarter.

For the full year, we are reaffirming our guidance for net sales growth of 6-8%, organic growth of 5-7%, and adjusted diluted EPS of $5.50 to $5.70.

Now, let's open the call for questions.

**Operator:**  
[Operator instructions.] Our first question comes from John Smith with Goldman Sachs. Please proceed.

**John Smith (Goldman Sachs):**  
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of inflation on your business?

**Alex Rivera (CEO):**  
Good morning, John. Inflation remains a challenge, particularly in commodities like cocoa, dairy, and palm oil, but as I outlined in our pricing and RGM discussion, we've offset it effectively with targeted 6.1% increases calibrated by our AI pricing engine, maintaining resilient elasticities around -1.8 and positive volumes. This has protected margins while driving mix to premium SKUs.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Maria Lopez with Morgan Stanley. Please proceed.

**Maria Lopez (Morgan Stanley):**  
What are your plans for HydraFuel and what is the expected impact of the product?

**Lisa Chen (Chief Growth Officer):**  
Thanks, Maria. HydraFuel, our electrolyte line, is a cornerstone of our hydration portfolio. We've expanded distribution to 2,500 new Walmart and Kroger doors, driving 14% growth this quarter through health halo positioning. Expect it to contribute 200-300 basis points to beverages volume in FY24, with e-com acceleration mirroring post-pandemic trends like Gatorade, and margins expanding via supply efficiencies.

**Operator:**  
Our next question comes from Bob Johnson with Barclays. Please proceed.

**Bob Johnson (Barclays):**  
How are you managing supply chain disruptions?

**David Patel (Chief Supply Chain Officer):**  
Great question, Bob. Disruptions from commodity volatility and logistics persist, but our AI demand forecasting has improved inventory turns 15% and stockouts 22%. We've boosted hedging 20% on cocoa, coffee, palm, rice; invested in cold-chain with Swiggy in APAC and micro-depots in LATAM for 8% rural gains; and BevOptix ERP for efficiency. This ensures 95% OOS recovery and resilience like peers.

**Operator:**  
Thank you. Our next question comes from Sarah Jenkins with GreenCapital Partners. Please proceed.

**Sarah Jenkins (GreenCapital Partners):**  
Thanks, and good morning, team. I wanted to dive into your sustainability progress. With EU regulations tightening under the Green Deal and consumer premiums for eco-labeled products hitting 15-20% in recent Nielsen surveys, can you update us on key initiatives and how they're tracking against your 2030 goals?

**Alex Rivera (CEO):**  
Great question, Sarah, and one we get a lot from investors focused on ESG. Sustainability is core to our long-term value in F&B, where supply resilience and loyalty matter most. It's in our FY24 priorities, with strong progress on four pillars: sustainable sourcing, emissions, water, circular packaging.

Sustainable sourcing at 78% verified for cocoa/palm/coffee/dairy, up from 62%, ahead 75% FY24 target and Mondelez. Regenerative Ag 450k hectares Savanna Institute; NA Midwest corn 30% no-till +1.2t C/ha Control Union; Europe 92% RSPO palm EU Deforestation; APAC 150 smallholder blockchain tea 100% deforest-free Nestle-style.

Emissions Scope 1/2 -22% 1.45M tCO2e to SBTi 45% 2030; Scope 3 -18% supplier push, 65% renewable, LATAM solar 40% Pepsi-like. Memphis digesters 95% methane 15% energy ROI <3yr.

Water +28% efficiency 1.8L/L >25% goal; India Rajasthan 98% ZLD IDE; 55% sites positive $12M CA aquifers.

Packaging 62% recyclable up 48%, rPET TerraSparkle -35k tons virgin EU/NA; UK Loop -40% single-use; landfill 4.5% food waste 92% Too Good To Go.

Europe 95% CSRD +8% organic sales; NA Green Thumb TerraBars +5 IRI; APAC/LATAM scaling $50M palm. $145M savings NPS +12% Gen Z 35% vol. Diversified cocoa buffer. Net-zero 2042, 100% sustainable 2030, $1B green capex hydrogen. Scope 3 transport +3% freight issue, CDP A-list.

**Operator:**  
Our last question comes from Chris Lee with JPMorgan. Please proceed.

**Chris Lee (JPMorgan):**  
What is your outlook for the rest of the year?

**Michael Thompson (CFO):**  
Thanks, Chris. We're optimistic for Q4 and full year, with organic growth 5-7% as Alex noted, led by APAC/EMEA easier comps. RGM supports 7-9% revenue, margins expanding on efficiencies. FY guide reaffirmed: sales 6-8%, organic 5-7%, EPS $5.50-5.70. Monitoring consumer sentiment but positioned via premiumization, innovation, share gains.

**Operator:**  
I would now like to turn the call back over to Alex Rivera for closing remarks.

**Alex Rivera (CEO):**  
Thank you for your questions and your continued interest in VitaFlavor Inc. We are focused on executing our strategy and delivering strong results. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

**Operator:**  
This concludes today's conference call. Thank you for your participation. You may now disconnect.
